summary:
Lunar Site Check is an interactive tool for rapidly comparing lunar landing sites and dates, with an emphasis on the Moon’s south pole. Users can select curated sites or enter custom coordinates, adjust a 30-day timeline, and compare Sun illumination and Earth visibility side by side. A 2D horizon view and optional 3D Moon visualization help explain how terrain affects sunlight and direct-to-Earth communication. Users can set screening thresholds for usable sunlight and communication outages, inspect estimated operational windows, and share scenarios or export hourly data.

The app calculates topocentric Sun and Earth positions using astronomy-engine; selected results were spot-checked against NASA/JPL Horizons. NASA NSSDC landing-site coordinates inform the curated list. Terrain profiles can be supplied from LOLA data, but none are bundled, so sites without a profile use a flat-horizon assumption. This tool supports rapid preliminary comparisons, not mission-certified power or communications analysis.
details:
Lunar Site Check helps mission planners, educators, and the public quickly compare lunar landing-site and date options. Users can select curated locations—including southern lunar sites—or enter custom coordinates, set a UTC start date, and explore a 30-day period with a playback timeline. Side-by-side scenarios show Sun and Earth azimuth and elevation, visibility statistics, upcoming sunlight and communication windows, and whether user-defined screening thresholds are met. Results can be shared by link or exported as hourly CSV data.

The application calculates topocentric Sun and Earth positions with astronomy-engine, including lunar body rotation and parallax. Selected results were spot-checked against NASA/JPL Horizons. NASA NSSDC landing-site coordinates inform the curated site list. Users can provide horizon profiles as JSON, and a Python workflow is included to generate profiles from LOLA elevation data. No LOLA masks are bundled, so locations without a profile use a flat-horizon assumption. Mission pass/fail results are preliminary screening indicators, not a spacecraft power, thermal, or communications-link model.

The project was built with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Three.js, with Python tooling for terrain-profile processing. Its creative approach combines 2D horizon plots, an interactive 3D lunar view, mission thresholds, and time-window comparisons in one accessible bilingual interface. The intended impact is to make schedule and site trade-offs easier to explore when mission plans change.
